what_its_for: Cilostazol is used to treat a condition called intermittent claudication. This means you get leg pain, cramping, or tiredness when you walk because not enough blood is reaching your leg muscles. This medicine helps improve blood flow in your legs so you can walk farther and with less pain.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Take it on an EMPTY stomach, at least 30 minutes BEFORE or 2 hours AFTER eating a meal. Do not crush or chew the tablet. Try to take it at the same times every day to help you remember.
dosing: The usual dose is 100 mg taken TWICE a day (once in the morning and once in the evening). Your doctor may start you on a lower dose of 50 mg twice a day if you are also taking certain other medications. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, skip it and take your next scheduled dose at the regular time. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for the missed one. Just continue your regular dosing schedule.
storage: Store cilostazol tablets at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Store in the original container with the cap tightly closed. Keep all medicines safely out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice while taking this medicine, as it can increase the amount of drug in your body and raise your risk of side effects. Avoid smoking, as it reduces the effectiveness of this medicine. Limit or avoid alcohol, as it may lower your blood pressure too much. Be cautious with aspirin and other blood thinners unless your doctor has specifically told you to take them together.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away or call 911 if you experience: chest pain or a fast or irregular heartbeat, shortness of breath or difficulty breathing, sudden numbness or weakness on one side of your body, sudden severe headache, vision changes, or signs of bleeding such as unusual bruising, blood in your urine or stool, or coughing up blood. Also call your doctor if you develop a fever, swollen lymph nodes, easy bruising, or if you feel faint or dizzy.
when_it_works: You may begin to notice some improvement in how far you can walk within 2 to 4 weeks of starting this medicine. However, it may take up to 12 weeks (about 3 months) before you feel the full benefit. Keep taking it regularly even if you do not feel better right away. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: HEART FAILURE: This medicine should NOT be used if you have heart failure of any kind. Please tell your doctor if you have or have ever had heart failure. PREGNANCY AND BREASTFEEDING: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as the safety of this medicine has not been fully established. KIDNEY OR LIVER DISEASE: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems, as your dose may need to be adjusted. OLDER ADULTS: Older patients can generally take this medicine at the standard dose, but should be monitored closely for side effects.
